title: Wall work-block thickness by building type
statement: For each selected building outline, the user chooses the building type. A house gets a wall band 0.302 m thick, a garage 0.215 m thick. If no type is chosen, House applies.

evidence.detail: cond on the keyword answer sets thickness 0.302 or 0.215
v0.6 note: all buildings selected together get the same thickness

authority.basis: 0.302 m and 0.215 m match common UK wall build-ups (cavity wall, one-brick wall); not stated in the source

uncertainty: Whether the values come from a standard, a client requirement or the author's practice
required_human_ruling: Confirm the two thicknesses and their source; are other building types needed?

title: Building outline is the outer face of the external wall
statement: The selected outline is treated as the outer face of the external wall: a copy is offset inwards by half the wall thickness and drawn with a constant width equal to the thickness, so the band covers the wall between the outline and the inner face.
dependencies: DT:InnerPoint (0 - Function library.lsp) to find a point inside the outline

evidence.detail: offset by dist = 0.5 * thickness towards DT:InnerPoint, then ConstantWidth = thickness

authority.basis: representation convention of the set-out drawing

uncertainty: DT:InnerPoint may fail on non-convex outlines (L-shaped houses); behaviour not observed

title: Set-out and work-block layers
statement: The original outline is closed if open, given zero width and ByLayer colour, and placed on layer 'e-set-out-house'; the wall band goes on layer 'e-work-block'. Both layers are created in colour 7 if missing.

evidence.detail: tblsearch/-layer creation; vla-put-layer for outline and copy

authority.basis: layer names follow a firm prefix scheme (e-...)

required_human_ruling: In a new platform, map the two layers to categories or keep them as named layers?
